title: 5th Sitting of third session of 2025
presiding: Speaker Abdul Raheem Abdulla (Fonadhoo); Deputy Speaker Ahmed Nazim chaired after the 10:30-11:01 break
summary: The sitting opened at 9:01 with committee changes, committee deadlines and a first reading of a human organ transplant bill. Most of the morning went on the continued debate of a motion calling for faster action on corruption flagged in the Auditor General's special audit of Fenaka Corporation, with ruling-party members stressing past losses and opposition members calling for even-handed action and pointing to current-government cases. Two audit and state-company bills then closed without further debate, and Dr. Shamheed (South Hulhumale') argued the Speaker was running the Majlis contrary to Article 98 of the Constitution over ministers not being summoned; the Speaker said sittings follow the rules. After the break, committee reports on integrity commission members and ambassadors were closed to debate pending votes. The text layer is fairly garbled, so some speaker gists are approximate and the attendance count of 35 present is as printed. This part opens with the end of the debate on the General Committee's report on dress rules for sittings (an amendment to Rule 61), then a debate on the committee's report on adding a chapter to the Majlis Rules for public-opinion votes under Act 2025/15. After a break from 11:53 to 13:00 the Speaker took 14 votes: the dress amendments and the amended dress report passed, the public-opinion chapter passed 42-0 with 1 abstention, two bills were accepted and sent to the Finance Committee along with a resolution on the Fenaka Corporation audit, and four National Integrity Commission nominees, two ambassadors and a treaty instrument were approved. The next sitting was set for Tuesday 14 October 2025 at 9:00. The text layer is garbled in places and the first speech (a continuation from part 1, with no header here) could not be attributed, so speaker gists are approximate.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Said this government is investigating past cases and called for audits of all councils, including Addu City funds.
Raised a point of order objecting to claims that the Speaker breaches the rules.
Said integrity commissions and others must also be monitored, citing Addu City council spending.
As a General Committee member, said the amendment was needed because some members dressed contrary to the Rules and to Maldivian office norms.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Backed closing loopholes in financial declaration laws and passing an asset recovery law.
Argued the Speaker runs the Majlis contrary to Article 98 of the Constitution because ministers are not summoned, and cited rules 42, 43 and 81.

speakers.name: Mohamed Shahid
positions: Cited large Fenaka invoices, said trust in the company has been lost, and denied the probes are political revenge.
Presented the General Committee report on Rule 61 (dress code) amendment.
Presented the General Committee report on adding a chapter after Chapter 51 of the Rules setting how the Majlis acts on public-opinion votes, saying committee members agreed unanimously.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Raised a point of order saying the rules do not require evidence to be submitted with an urgent matter.
Said the dress amendment compels members to wear ties even though some media say it does not, and that dignity cannot be forced.
Said ministers summoned under the Rules do not attend, and members should hold the government accountable instead.
Said he is in a minority party whose proposals in committee are not acted on, and his constituents want him to speak for their rights.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Supported prompt audits but said one-off special audits are not enough; urged updating audit reports and referral to the ACC.
Said he did not support the Rule 61 dress amendment and that the Rules already require ministers to appear within 14 days, which he said is not being met.
Said questions sent to ministers on 27 November 2024 were unanswered, so Majlis dignity depends on holding ministers to account, not on ties.
Raised two 40-foot containers reported lost from state custody and asked who is responsible.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said the debate strayed from the motion and alleged selective prosecution, citing the MDP chair's ACC summons and other pending cases.
Questioned adding another chapter to the Rules while, he said, the Majlis shows little respect for its own institution and integrity.
Said a nominee rejected by a committee had been sent again, and called for ministers to be made to appear in the chamber.

speakers.name: Ahmed Xamyr
positions: Backed the motion and asked why former officials did not pursue cases while in office; discussed housing flat allocation.
Said land and flat allocations should also be audited and prosecuted.

speakers.name: Ahmed Naseer
positions: Called for audits of all islands and companies and scrutiny of Fenaka supplier bills before further payments.
Seconded Ashraf Rasheed's second amendment on dress at oath and presidential address sittings.

speakers.name: Mohamed Dawoodh
positions: Presented the Foreign Relations committee report on non-resident ambassadors, passed unanimously in committee.
Presented the committee report on accepting the 1986 Constitutional Amendment instrument, passed unanimously in committee.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Began remarks on the Rule 61 report, noting earlier committee reports had drawn no debate (continues in the next part).
Supported the report, saying public-opinion votes matter because conditions differ across atolls.
Said the President travels to islands to hear residents, and expressed surprise that MDP members did not back the measure.

speakers.name: Ashraf Rasheed
positions: Proposed that official dress mean coat, trousers and tie, or shirt, tie and trousers, or national dress, with women's dress following general decency norms.
Proposed that at oath-taking and the President's address, male members wear coat, trousers and tie or national dress, and women coat or trousers or national dress.

speakers.name: Hussain Sameer
positions: Backed action on the Fenaka audit but said it covers one period and urged equal action on cases under all governments.
Criticised the current government over police and state-company matters.

speakers.name: Hassan Zareer
positions: Said the Fenaka audit shows large losses that went uninvestigated earlier, and urged tighter procurement and legal reform.

speakers.name: Ahmed Aifan
positions: Said the Fenaka theft claims are not new and the government is now investigating, while protests aim to stop probes.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Muhammad
positions: Said audits should be routine and urged dealing with the findings rather than blaming the Auditor General or Police Commissioner.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Called on the ACC to act on alleged 2019-2023 thefts and for laws to be enforced so losses are recovered.

speakers.name: Abdul Sattar Mohamed
positions: Cited inflated purchases, said corruption should be probed under any government, and called for an integrity-testing mechanism and asset recovery law.

speakers.name: Abdulla Shareef
positions: Presented the committee report recommending four National Integrity Commission members who scored over 75 percent.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Said members should attend in coat and trousers, or shirt, tie and trousers, and he did not accept looser forms such as national dress as drafted.
Said the dress rule should stay as the clauses set out, and spoke about the standard of dress expected of members.

speakers.name: Anara Naeem
positions: Supported the report, saying seeking people's views is important for the state and for governing well.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said seeking public views is fine but asked whether the government does so, citing equipment moved from Hanimaadhoo airport before its 9 November opening.
Raised the lost cigarette containers and asked for the responsible people to be found.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ismail
positions: Seconded Ashraf Rasheed's first amendment to the dress rule.

decisions: Urgent matter from the Kendhoo member was not accepted because Rule 197 conditions were not met.
Ten Media and Broadcasting Commission applicants were sent to the Independent Institutions Committee.
Two Independent Institutions Committee seat changes and three committee bill deadlines were announced.
Human organ transplantation bill had its first reading.
Debate on the Fenaka audit motion, the Audit Act amendment bill and the state-business law amendment bill was closed with no closing remarks from sponsors.
Reports on integrity commission members, non-resident ambassadors and the 1986 constitutional amendment instrument were closed to debate; votes set for voting time.
Debate on the dress-rule report closed because no further members wished to speak.
Two floor amendments to Rule 61 (official dress; dress at oath and presidential address sittings) passed.
The General Committee report on the dress rules, as amended, passed 48-0; the Speaker asked members to follow it and to wear a tie or leave if not.
The chapter on public-opinion votes was added to the Majlis Rules (42 yes, 0 no, 1 abstained).
The Fenaka Corporation audit resolution was accepted and sent to the Finance Committee.
The Audit Act (2007/4) amendment bill and the Act 2013/3 amendment bill (state businesses privatisation, corporatisation and monitoring) were accepted and sent to the Finance Committee.
Four National Integrity Commission nominees were approved: Fathimath Shareef, Shifaaz Ali, Shuaib Abdul Rahman and Ali Mohamed Manik.
Ambassador Aishath Azeema (India, also non-resident to Kazakhstan) and Masood Imaad (Sri Lanka, also non-resident to Mauritius) were approved.
The Majlis accepted the Instrument for the Acceptance of the 1986 Constitutional Amendment.
The sitting closed; the next sitting is Tuesday 14 October 2025 at 9:00.
